#### Why the outside world cannot be recomputed, and what follows from that

**A side effect touches the outside world, and the outside world has no "recompute".** Retry the aggregation and window [12:08, 12:10) is 8 again, because the state is a function of the records. Retry `charge(order 4, 6)` and the card is charged **12**, because the money moved and nothing in the pipeline records that it did.

Worse, the pipeline **cannot tell**: a charge that timed out after succeeding looks exactly like one that failed. So it has only two options, and they are the same option — make the effect safe to repeat, or ask the external system whether it already happened.

**An idempotency key is how you ask.** First attempt: `charge("order-4", 6)`, the processor records the key and charges 6. The pipeline crashes before committing. The retry sends the same call, the processor **recognises the key**, and the total charged is 6.

Note what the key does *not* do: it does not make the effect idempotent. It moves the deduplication to the only place that can see both attempts. Two requirements follow — the key must be derived from the **data** (a key generated at send time is a second charge with extra steps), and the external system has to offer the feature at all.

**And here is where the previous concept's redundancy disappears.** There are 3 ways a failure after the first charge can send order 4 again, and with no guard each one charges 12:

- **upstream crash, shuffle alive** — the upstream stage dies after sending and re-sends on restart; the shuffle never crashed, still holds the id, and drops the copy. Dedup: covers. Key: covers.
- **charge timeout, retried by the sink** — the call succeeded but its reply was lost, so the sink retries it from AFTER the dedup point and the copy never passes the shuffle. Dedup: **misses**. Key: covers.
- **crash after the charge, before the offset commit** — the seen-set dies with the process, the replay re-reads the record and it looks new; only the external system knows the charge happened. Dedup: **misses**. Key: covers.

A deduplicating shuffle covers **1 of 3**; an idempotency key covers **3 of 3**. For a pure aggregation the two guards were interchangeable. For a side effect only the external one reaches the crash windows that matter.

**Placement helps too, and it is free.** In a 4-stage pipeline (source → shuffle → aggregate → sink), an effect at stage 2 can be re-run by a crash in 3 stages; at the last stage, only 1. That is a 3× reduction in exposure from placement alone, and it keeps everything upstream pure and freely retryable.

#### When each mechanism applies, and the one you cannot provide yourself

**Use an idempotency key whenever the external system offers one** — Stripe, most payment processors, any API with an `Idempotency-Key` header, any database with upsert. It is one round trip, the retry is free, and the decision is made by the only component that can make it.

**Push the effect to the last stage, always.** It costs nothing, reduces exposure 3× here, and leaves the computation above it pure — so the expensive part of the pipeline can be retried without anyone thinking about it.

**Reach for two-phase commit only when there is no key.** It genuinely achieves exactly-once across an external effect, and it has a state — prepared, coordinator gone — in which neither committing nor aborting is safe. That state is resolved by a human, which is why it is the fallback rather than the default.

**What this does not settle, and it is a dependency rather than a gap:** the whole mechanism rests on a feature of someone else's system. If the processor has no idempotency key, this design does not degrade — it is unavailable. And if the key is generated at send time rather than derived from the order, the pipeline looks correct and double-charges, with nothing inside it able to detect the difference.

<details>
<summary><b>Step 1 of 4</b> — a side effect cannot be recomputed</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch05-effects/frames/step-01.svg" alt="Step 1: a side effect cannot be recomputed" width="1040">

The asymmetry is total. Recomputing window state gives 8 however many times you do it, because the state is a function of the records. Re-running a charge gives 12, because the money moved and nothing in the pipeline knows. And the pipeline cannot distinguish a timed-out charge that succeeded from one that failed — so it must either make repetition safe, or ask.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 2 of 4</b> — an idempotency key moves the dedup OUTSIDE</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch05-effects/frames/step-02.svg" alt="Step 2: an idempotency key moves the dedup OUTSIDE" width="1040">

An idempotency key does not make the effect idempotent — it moves the deduplication to the only place that can see both attempts. Two requirements follow, both in the note: the key must come from the data (a send-time key is useless), and the external system has to support it. The second is a dependency you cannot work around from inside.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 3 of 4</b> — so dedup covers 1 of 3 crash windows, the key covers 3</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch05-effects/frames/step-03.svg" alt="Step 3: so dedup covers 1 of 3 crash windows, the key covers 3" width="1040">

This is the concept's whole argument in one table. For a pure aggregation, dedup and an idempotent sink were interchangeable. For a side effect they are not: dedup covers only a copy that comes back THROUGH a shuffle that still remembers the id. A retry issued after the dedup point, and a replay after the seen-set died with the process, are reachable only by the external system's own key. 1 of 3 against 3 of 3.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 4 of 4</b> — and isolating the effect at the boundary shrinks its exposure</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch05-effects/frames/step-04.svg" alt="Step 4: and isolating the effect at the boundary shrinks its exposure" width="1040">

Placement is the cheapest of the three mechanisms and the only one that needs no cooperation. An effect at stage 2 can be re-run by a crash in 3 stages; at stage 4 only 1 can reach it — a 3× reduction. And everything upstream stays pure, which means it can be retried without a thought.

</details>
